issues.t: Cranks but won't start, often when hot
issues.sym: The engine turns over but won't fire, or it stalls and won't restart until it cools down. You may not hear the fuel pump hum when you turn the key.
issues.why: The fuel-injection main relay on Hondas of this era develops cracked solder joints that lose contact when warm, cutting power to the fuel pump. A failing distributor igniter or coil can cause the same kind of no-start.
issues.next: Have a shop check for fuel pump power and spark while the problem is happening. A main relay or distributor part is usually the fix.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Delayed or harsh shifts, engine revs flaring between gears, slipping, or the car refusing to move in drive.
issues.why: The automatic used in this generation wears internally, and failures are the most-reported problem for these years, especially 2001 and 2002.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition right away. If it is slipping or won't engage, stop driving it hard and get a transmission diagnosis; a rebuild or replacement is usually needed.

issues.t: Airbag (SRS) light on from passenger seat sensor
issues.sym: The SRS airbag warning light stays on.
issues.why: The occupant position detection sensor in the passenger seat can fault. Honda extended the warranty on this sensor and its control unit to 10 years or 150,000 miles on 2001-2003 and some 2004 Civics.
issues.next: Have the SRS codes read. Airbags may not deploy correctly while the light is on, so get it fixed and ask a Honda dealer whether the extended coverage still applies.

issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifold
issues.sym: A ticking or hissing noise when accelerating, a louder exhaust, exhaust smell, a check engine light, or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: The exhaust manifold on the 1.7L engine is prone to cracking from repeated heating and cooling.
issues.next: Have the manifold inspected. Exhaust leaks near the engine can let fumes into the cabin, so do not put this off.

issues.t: Head gasket leak and overheating
issues.sym: Temperature gauge climbing, coolant disappearing, white exhaust smoke, or bubbles in the coolant reservoir.
issues.why: Head gasket leaks are a known weak point on this generation and are often triggered or worsened by overheating.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine overheats. Have a cooling system pressure test and combustion leak test done before the head is damaged.

issues.t: Hybrid (IMA) battery weakening
issues.sym: IMA warning light, weak or missing electric assist, the battery gauge dropping quickly, and worse fuel economy.
issues.why: The hybrid battery pack in early Civic Hybrids loses capacity with age. Honda issued bulletins and a warranty extension for the IMA battery module on these years.
issues.next: Have the hybrid system scanned by a Honda dealer or hybrid specialist and ask whether any extended coverage applies.
src: Honda warranty extension A12-077 (IMA battery, 2003-2008 Civic Hybrid)

issues.t: Cracked engine block coolant leak
issues.sym: Coolant loss with no visible hose leak, coolant seeping near the back of the engine, or overheating.
issues.why: A casting flaw lets the engine block crack. Honda extended the engine block warranty to 10 years for 2006-2008 and some early 2009 Civics; that coverage has largely run out.
issues.next: Stop driving if it overheats. Watch the coolant level closely and, when buying, ask for proof the block was replaced.

issues.t: Rapid or uneven rear tire wear
issues.sym: Rear tires wear on the inner edge or develop a cupped pattern, causing a roar or vibration at highway speed.
issues.why: The rear suspension holds too much camber. Honda released new rear upper control arms and extended coverage on them for some 2006-2008 models.
issues.next: Have the alignment checked and ask a Honda dealer about the rear control arm kit from the service bulletin.

issues.t: Electric power steering feels heavy
issues.sym: Steering suddenly feels stiff or hard to turn, especially at low speed.
issues.why: The electric power steering system on 2006-2009 Civic Si and 2006-2007 Civic Hybrid models can fail. Honda extended the steering warranty to 10 years or 150,000 miles on those cars.
issues.next: Have the steering system checked and ask a Honda dealer whether your car falls under the extended coverage.

issues.t: Knock or clunk from torn engine mount
issues.sym: Clunk or rattle from the right front over bumps, plus extra vibration at idle.
issues.why: The passenger-side fluid-filled engine mount tears and leaks.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected and replace any that are torn or leaking.

issues.t: Paint cracking or clear coat peeling
issues.sym: Fine cracks, dull patches, or peeling clear coat on the hood, roof, and front fenders.
issues.why: Paint durability problems on this generation. Honda issued a paint warranty extension for hood and fender cracking.
issues.next: Cosmetic. Ask a Honda dealer about the paint bulletin; otherwise repaint as needed.

issues.t: CVT drive pulley damage (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of drive power or the car not moving, sometimes after hard acceleration from a stop.
issues.why: The original CVT control software could overload the drive pulley shaft and crack it. Honda recalled these cars to update the software.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the update done before driving more.

issues.t: Fuel in the engine oil (oil dilution)
issues.sym: Oil level rising on the dipstick, a gas smell from the oil, or rough running, mostly in cold weather with short trips.
issues.why: Fuel washes past the piston rings into the oil when the turbo engine never fully warms up. Honda issued software updates and extended warranty coverage on related engine parts.
issues.next: Check the oil level regularly, keep up with oil changes, and ask a Honda dealer about the software update and extended coverage.

issues.t: A/C stops blowing cold (condenser leak)
issues.sym: Air from the vents turns warm or only slightly cool.
issues.why: The A/C condenser in front of the radiator can leak refrigerant. Honda extended condenser coverage to 10 years with no mileage limit on these Civics.
issues.next: Have the A/C leak-tested and ask a Honda dealer whether the condenser is covered.

issues.t: Fuel pump may fail (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, sputtering, the engine stalling while driving, or not starting.
issues.why: A defective low-pressure fuel pump in some cars can stop working.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls (21V-215, 20V-314 and 23V-858 cover different build ranges) and get the pump replaced. A stall at speed is a crash risk.

issues.t: Sticky or heavy steering (recall)
issues.sym: Steering feels notchy, sticks, or takes more effort to turn, especially at certain angles.
issues.why: A part in the steering gearbox can deform and create friction. Honda recalled these cars to install a new steering part.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and schedule the repair promptly. If the steering is noticeably hard to turn, limit driving until it is fixed.

issues.t: Brake booster check valve can stick (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels unusually hard and the car takes more leg effort to stop, sometimes only now and then.
issues.why: A soapy assembly lubricant left on the brake booster check valve can make the valve stick, which cuts the power assist to the brakes.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 96V-106. If the pedal turns hard, leave extra stopping room and have the booster valve checked before regular driving.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not deploy properly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can see or feel. The risk is a passenger airbag that does not open the way it should in a crash.
issues.why: Some passenger airbag modules were put together incorrectly at the factory. This is separate from the later airbag inflator recalls.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 97V-193 and have the module repaired before carrying a front passenger regularly.

issues.t: Ignition switch can wear and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine cuts out suddenly while driving, sometimes with the dash lights flickering, and may restart right away as if nothing happened.
issues.why: The electrical contacts inside the ignition switch wear down and can briefly lose connection, which shuts the engine off.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 02V-120 and have the switch replaced. A stall in traffic is a crash risk, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Driver-side driveshaft can separate (recall)
issues.sym: The car suddenly stops pulling even though the engine revs, or it rolls when parked in gear without the parking brake set.
issues.why: Some driver-side driveshafts were assembled without a properly seated retaining clip, so the shaft can pull out of its joint.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 12V-256. Always set the parking brake until the driveshaft has been inspected.

issues.t: Fuel feed line seal may leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell around the engine bay, sometimes with a damp spot on the fuel line.
issues.why: On a small batch of early cars, a rubber sealing ring in the fuel feed line was seated crooked and can let a little fuel seep out.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 11V-288. Do not drive with a fuel smell until the line is checked.

issues.t: Steering column may not absorb crash forces (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing shows up in normal driving. The concern is how the steering column behaves in a frontal crash.
issues.why: A few cars built over several days received the wrong steering column bracket, so the column may not collapse the way it was designed to.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 12V-548 and have the column inspected at a Honda dealer.

issues.t: Piston pin clip may be missing on the 2.0L (recall)
issues.sym: A sudden knocking from the engine, loss of power, or the engine locking up while driving.
issues.why: On early-build 2.0L engines, a small clip that holds the piston pin in place may be missing or not seated. The pin can drift and wreck the cylinder, and a seized engine can also cause a fire.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 16V-074. If the engine starts knocking, stop driving and have the car towed.

issues.t: Electric parking brake may not set (recall)
issues.sym: A brake warning light after shutting the car off, and the parking brake not holding when it is applied right after the ignition is turned off.
issues.why: The original brake control software may not apply the electric parking brake if the switch is pulled just after the car is switched off.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 16V-725. Until the update is done, set the parking brake before turning the car off and leave the shifter in Park.

issues.t: Right axle shaft may break (recall)
issues.sym: A sudden loss of drive power, or the car rolling when parked without the parking brake set.
issues.why: Some right-side axle shafts were not heat-treated correctly and can snap under load.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 17V-706. Use the parking brake every time you park until the shaft is inspected.

issues.t: Steering assist can push the wrong way at full lock (recall)
issues.sym: When the wheel is turned all the way to its stop, such as while parking, the steering may tug in an unexpected direction.
issues.why: A magnet in the steering torque sensor can come loose, so the electric power steering misreads what the driver is doing.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 18V-663 and have the steering gearbox replaced if your car is covered.

issues.t: Passenger seat sensor can crack and set off the airbag (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light, or in the worst case a passenger airbag that goes off when it should not.
issues.why: The weight sensor in the front passenger seat can crack and short out, which confuses the airbag system.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 26V-332 and 24V-064. If the airbag light is on, have it checked before carrying a front passenger.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder can separate from the booster (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels different, travels farther than normal, or braking power drops sharply.
issues.why: A fastener that holds the brake master cylinder to the booster may have been put together wrong at the factory and can come loose.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 23V-458. Any change in pedal feel means the car should be inspected before it is driven further.

issues.t: Steering rack may let a front tire rub (recall)
issues.sym: A rubbing sound when turning, or scuff marks and damage on the inner edge of a front tire.
issues.why: Some electric power steering racks were assembled incorrectly, which can let a front tire touch nearby parts and wear through.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 23V-704 and look over the front tires for scuffing. A damaged tire should be replaced before driving at speed.

issues.t: Driver seat frame may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: The driver seat cushion rocks, shifts or clunks when you brake, accelerate or get in and out.
issues.why: The seat cushion frame may not have been fastened properly at the factory, so the seat is not fully secured in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 24V-859 and have the seat frame replaced if your car is included.

issues.t: Stability control unit may leak brake fluid (recall)
issues.sym: A low brake fluid warning, a soft pedal, or stability control and ABS lights.
issues.why: A valve inside the stability control (VSA) hydraulic unit can leak brake fluid internally.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 23V-430. Do not keep driving with a soft pedal or a brake warning light.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump may crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw fuel smell while driving or at idle, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: The high-pressure fuel pump on the hybrid engine can crack and let gasoline escape near hot parts, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 24V-763. If you smell fuel, park outside and have the car inspected before driving it again.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture or underinflate (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you can see day to day; the problem only appears when the airbag is needed.
issues.why: The driver airbag inflator can take in moisture over the years, so it may burst or fire with too little force.
issues.next: Have the VIN checked and the inflator replaced; this is free and the airbag is the part meant to save you.

issues.t: Accessory floor mat can hold the accelerator down (recall)
issues.sym: The pedal does not come back to idle when you lift your foot, or the engine keeps revving.
issues.why: The dealer-fitted driver floor mat can shift forward and sit under the accelerator pedal.
issues.next: Take the mat out now and have the correct mat and clip fitted; a stuck throttle is a crash risk.

issues.t: Rear seat belt buckle can be hard to release (recall)
issues.sym: A rear seat belt buckle will not unlatch easily, or takes several tries to release.
issues.why: Some rear buckle assemblies were made out of spec, so the release button can bind.
issues.next: Have the buckles replaced under the campaign, because a jammed buckle traps a passenger after a crash.

issues.t: Factory-mounted tire can lose air from a damaged bead (recall)
issues.sym: A tire keeps going soft, the pressure light comes on, or a tire goes flat for no clear reason.
issues.why: The bead of the tire can be pinched while it is mounted at the factory, which lets air escape.
issues.next: Have the tires inspected under the campaign and do not keep topping up a tire that will not hold air.
